name: Cris Collinsworth
blurb: Talks through the replay like a film session and loves to single out one player to explain a play.

quotes.q: The Bears' season's gonna end on a double doink.
quotes.ctx: Jan 6, 2019 wild card, Eagles at Bears (with Al Michaels): Cody Parkey's last-second kick hit the upright and then the crossbar, and the phrase became the name of the play.

quotes.q: I'm sorry, but I can't believe the call.
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl XLIX, Feb 1, 2015: Seattle threw from the 1-yard line instead of handing to Marshawn Lynch, and Malcolm Butler intercepted it.

quotes.q: Well, I guess they're going to have to overturn this one.
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl LII, Feb 2018, on the review of Zach Ertz's go-ahead touchdown; the touchdown stood, and he later said he wished he had not said it.

quotes.q: That is an absolutely terrible call that's going to decide this football game!
quotes.ctx: Lions at Eagles, Sunday Night Football, Nov 2025, on a late pass interference flag against Detroit.

quotes.q: If this were Patrick Mahomes we'd be screaming, 'Oh Patrick Mahomes!'
quotes.ctx: Week 17 Bears-49ers Sunday night game, after Brock Purdy scrambled for over eight seconds before a touchdown pass; a joke at his own expense.

terms.means: His go-to way of starting a point about a player; fans have turned it into a drinking game.
At the open of the broadcast he slides into the camera shot from the side to join his partner; it became a meme in December 2018.
He is the longtime owner of Pro Football Focus, the service that grades every player on every play, and he cites its numbers on air.
He is known for gushing over Patrick Mahomes and has joked about it on air himself.

name: Tom Brady
blurb: Blunt quarterback's-eye view; he says plainly when a throw or a call was bad.

quotes.q: Poor awareness. Poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub.
quotes.ctx: Chargers at Bills, Sept 27, 2026, on a fourth-quarter Justin Herbert interception.

quotes.q: Don't like that one bit. This is too critical of a game.
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl LIX, Feb 2025: reacting to an offensive pass interference call on A.J. Brown.

quotes.q: You let the players play. It should be decided on the field.
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl LIX, Feb 2025: continuing on the same flag against A.J. Brown.

quotes.q: You don't ever get over them.
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl LIX, Feb 2025: on Super Bowl losses, as the Chiefs' defeat wound down.

quotes.q: Not a call I like at all.
quotes.ctx: 49ers at Eagles playoff game, Jan 11, 2026, on a personal foul after a late Jalen Hurts slide.

quotes.q: It's not that hard. Look off the safety and throw the seam.
quotes.ctx: Packers at Lions, Thanksgiving 2025, breaking down a 30-yard catch by Dontayvion Wicks.

terms.means: The award he hands out after each game he calls, to the player who fired him up the most; started in his first season, 2024.
His phrase for a soft, easy-to-intercept throw served up to the defense.
In his first season (2024) reviewers noted his loud, wordless reactions on big plays.

name: J.J. Watt
blurb: Conversational and funny, explains line play from a pass rusher's view; spent 2025 with Ian Eagle and moved up to the lead CBS booth in 2026.

quotes.q: Snip, snap, snip snap.
quotes.ctx: The first seconds of his CBS debut, Steelers at Jets, Sept 7, 2025: a line from The Office about the two quarterbacks swapping teams.

quotes.q: That was like a WWE heel turn!
quotes.ctx: Same debut game, after the referee corrected a penalty announcement.

quotes.q: The refs just changed the feeling of this entire building. Wow.
quotes.ctx: Same debut game, after the officiating mix-up swung the mood.

quotes.q: It couldn't have been his brother, because his brother catches those.
quotes.ctx: Same debut game, joking after his brother T.J. Watt batted down a pass.

quotes.q: Oh, my brothers are going to be pissed at me for that.
quotes.ctx: Same debut game, laughing at himself after mixing up Cam and Connor Heyward.

quotes.q: He just chucked it up there! And it stayed in the air forever!
quotes.ctx: His first game in the lead booth with Jim Nantz, Packers-Vikings, Sept 13, 2026, on a Kyler Murray interception under a blitz.

terms.means: When his brother T.J. Watt is playing he sometimes refers to him by jersey number to stay neutral.
He reaches for TV and wrestling references (The Office, a WWE heel turn) to describe what just happened.

name: Tony Romo
show: Lead CBS booth through the 2025 season
blurb: Excitable quarterback's-eye analyst who became famous for calling plays out loud before the snap; fans still quote him.

quotes.q: Rob Gronkowski is out wide. Watch the top of your screen. Watch this safety.
quotes.ctx: AFC Championship, Patriots at Chiefs, Jan 20, 2019: he said Brady would throw there if the safety came down, and Brady did.

quotes.q: Jim, I got five dollars this is a run to the left.
quotes.ctx: His first CBS broadcast, September 2017; the pre-snap guessing started on day one.

quotes.q: I feel like I'm watching American Beauty!
quotes.ctx: Bears at Packers, Sept 28, 2017, watching the wind whip during a lightning delay.

quotes.q: He'll be fine. I mean, he's Aaron Rodgers.
quotes.ctx: Bengals at Packers, Sept 24, 2017, late in a game Green Bay went on to win in overtime.

quotes.q: You got me with goose bumps, Nantz. That was unbelievable.
quotes.ctx: Commanders at Cowboys on Thanksgiving, praising his partner's call.

quotes.q: Oh my gosh, that was amazing!
quotes.ctx: AFC Championship, Chiefs at Ravens, Jan 2024, after a Patrick Mahomes pass to Travis Kelce.

terms.means: The nickname Jim Nantz gave him for predicting plays before the snap.
He constantly addressed his partner by name mid-thought, as in his debut-day "Jim, I got five dollars" line.
His frequent setup for declaring a play the turning point of a game.

name: Troy Aikman
blurb: Calm, direct, and increasingly willing to say exactly what he thinks, especially about officiating.

quotes.q: The product's just not very good. I'm gonna be honest.
quotes.ctx: Bengals at Broncos, Monday night, Sept 29, 2025: more than 20 penalties had been called by the third quarter.

quotes.q: I'm not gonna keep my mouth shut.
quotes.ctx: Same Bengals-Broncos game, before weighing in on yet another flag.

quotes.q: That's a good call. Just not a necessary call.
quotes.ctx: Same Bengals-Broncos game, finishing that thought.

quotes.q: Nothing brings a broadcast to a screeching halt more than these yellow flags.
quotes.ctx: Same Bengals-Broncos game.

quotes.q: The problem with all this is just make a call.
quotes.ctx: Packers at Giants, Dec 11, 2023, as officials took a long time over a kickoff ruling just before halftime.

quotes.q: But this is ridiculous what we're watching right now.
quotes.ctx: Same Packers-Giants delay.

terms.means: The word he reaches for when a penalty or a long review annoys him; it turns up in both of his best-known officiating rants.
How he describes his own style; partner Joe Buck says he now worries less about what people will think.

name: Kirk Herbstreit
played: QB, Ohio State (college); did not play in the NFL
blurb: College football's best-known analyst, also on ESPN's College GameDay; upbeat and coach-friendly.

name: Luke Kuechly
blurb: New in 2026; short, clear explanations from a linebacker's view of what the offense is trying to do. Debuted on the 49ers-Rams game from Australia.

terms.means: A reviewer of his debut noted he leans on this word a lot for players and tackles.

name: Greg Olsen
blurb: Teacher type who gets excited about strategy and clock management and explains it fast.

quotes.q: He's gotta get down! He's gotta get down!
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl LVII, Feb 2023: urging Chiefs RB Jerick McKinnon to stop short of the goal line to burn the clock; McKinnon did.

quotes.q: I'm aggressive by nature. Jason, I know we haven't worked a lot together.
quotes.ctx: Browns at Commanders, Oct 6, 2024, on a fourth-and-2 decision, to fill-in partner Jason Benetti.

terms.means: A phrase he said in a 2025 interview that he hates hearing from commentators and coaches; he thinks it makes no sense.

name: Drew Brees
blurb: Rejoined the booth in late 2025; easygoing delivery with detailed quarterback insight.

name: Jonathan Vilma
blurb: Explains the game from the defense's side.

name: Daryl Johnston
blurb: Longtime FOX voice with an old-school, blocking-and-toughness point of view.

terms.means: His nickname from his Cowboys days; partners still call him that on air.

name: Mark Schlereth
blurb: High-energy former lineman who focuses on the trenches.

terms.means: His nickname from his playing days in Washington, short for "stink head".

name: Ross Tucker
blurb: Former lineman and podcaster, promoted to the number two CBS crew in 2026.

name: Trent Green
blurb: Steady quarterback analysis next to Kevin Harlan's big calls.

name: Logan Ryan
blurb: Recently retired defensive back; new to this CBS crew in 2026.

name: Adam Archuleta
blurb: Low-key former safety who breaks down coverage.

name: Robert Turbin
played: RB, Seahawks 2012-14, later Browns, Cowboys, Colts
blurb: Former running back, new to a full-time CBS game crew in 2026.

name: John Madden
blurb: The most famous analyst ever: loud, funny sound effects on top of real teaching, and the name on the video game.

quotes.q: Boom!
quotes.ctx: His trademark shout on a big hit or block, used for decades.

quotes.q: Doink!
quotes.ctx: His sound effect for a ball bouncing off the goalpost; it is why a kick off the upright is called a doink.

quotes.q: See what it is, is it's a tethered blimp.
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl XXVI, Jan 1992, earnestly explaining the indoor blimp camera; a classic Madden tangent.

quotes.q: I would play for overtime.
quotes.ctx: Super Bowl XXXVI, Feb 3, 2002: with no timeouts he thought the Patriots should run out the clock; Tom Brady drove for the winning field goal instead.

quotes.q: What Tom Brady just did gives me goosebumps.
quotes.ctx: Same Super Bowl, moments later, after Brady's drive set up the winning kick.

terms.means: The interjections he punctuated replays with.
The on-screen pen he used to scribble circles and arrows over replays; he made it a TV staple.
A chicken inside a duck inside a turkey; he found it in New Orleans in 1997 and gave it to Thanksgiving game stars.
His shorthand for the catch rule: one knee down inbounds counts the same as two feet. He said it on a 1983 broadcast and made it a book title.
After the Thanksgiving game he handed drumsticks to the winners, sometimes from a turkey with up to eight legs.
His yearly list, started in 1984, of players who played the game the way he thought it should be played.
The custom bus he rode to every game from 1987 on because he would not fly.

name: Don Meredith
blurb: "Dandy Don", the folksy, joking counterweight to Howard Cosell on the original Monday Night Football.

quotes.q: Turn out the lights, the party's over.
quotes.ctx: The Willie Nelson line he would sing on Monday Night Football once he felt the game was decided.

terms.means: If he started singing it, he was telling you the game was over.
His nickname, used on air throughout his Monday Night Football years.
